column1: report
column4: reason

column1: Worker received a bruise to the shin after being brushed by a slow-moving golf cart in a walkway at very low speed.
column4: Low speed and minor contact meant limited transferred energy despite the line-of-fire exposure.

column1: Employee positioned himself between a reversing forklift and a fixed wall to guide the operator, with no spotter or horn signal used.
column4: Being pinned between a moving vehicle and a fixed structure is a well-known crushing fatality scenario.

column1: Reversing alarm and spotter were both used correctly while a forklift backed into a tight loading area with pedestrians nearby.
column4: Standard controls for vehicle line-of-fire hazards were followed correctly.

column1: A tensioned wire rope snapped during a rigging job and struck a support structure two metres from where a worker had been standing moments earlier.
column4: A whipping wire rope under tension can cause fatal or severe injury on release; the near-miss proximity confirms real exposure existed.

column1: Crew waited behind the marked barrier line while a jackhammer operator worked on a section of concrete slab ahead of them.
column4: Maintaining distance behind the barrier controlled the exposure to flying debris.

column1: Crane operator lifted a load exceeding the rated capacity for the current boom angle; the lift was completed without the load dropping.
column4: Exceeding rated lift capacity risks sudden structural failure of the crane or rigging, a major cause of fatal lifting incidents.

column1: Lift plan was reviewed, rigging inspected, and load weight confirmed against crane charts before a routine equipment lift.
column4: All standard lift-planning controls were completed correctly before the lift proceeded.

column1: Rigger used a sling with visible fraying to lift a moderately heavy steel beam; sling held for the duration of the lift.
column4: A visibly damaged sling can fail without warning during a lift, risking a dropped load onto personnel below.

column1: A tag line was used to control load rotation during a crane lift over an active work area, keeping the load steady throughout.
column4: Proper control measures reduced the risk of uncontrolled load movement.

column1: Two lifting points were used instead of the four specified in the rigging plan for an irregularly shaped load, lift proceeded without incident.
column4: Under-rigging an irregular load increases the chance of the load shifting or falling during the lift.

column1: Worker's hand was pinched between a pallet and a forklift fork while guiding a low, slow-speed lift in a warehouse aisle.
column4: Low lift height and slow speed limited the potential severity despite the injury that occurred.

column1: Crane was operated near an overhead power line without the required minimum clearance distance being confirmed beforehand.
column4: Contact between crane components and live power lines is a well-documented cause of multiple fatalities.

column1: Load chart and outrigger positioning were verified by a certified rigger before a crane lift near the edge of a slope.
column4: Certified verification of ground and rigging conditions controlled the primary tip-over hazard.

column1: Personnel remained under a raised forklift load while adjusting a strap, rather than lowering the load first.
column3: Line of Fire; Safe Mechanical Lifting
column4: Working beneath a suspended or raised load is a recurring precursor to fatal crush injuries.

column1: Lifting bag used to raise a section of pipe was rated well above the actual load weight, with a documented safety margin applied.
column4: Conservative capacity margin reduced the likelihood of equipment failure during the lift.

column1: Contractor began excavation work near a marked underground pipeline corridor without obtaining a permit or verifying utility locations.
column4: Unauthorized excavation near buried pipelines risks rupture of high-pressure or flammable lines, a known cause of fatal incidents.

column1: Permit to work was completed, reviewed by the area authority, and briefed to the full crew before maintenance began on a live process unit.
column4: Proper authorization and communication controls were in place before work started.

column1: Night shift crew continued a job past the permit's expiry time without renewing it, conditions in the area had not changed.
column4: Working outside a valid permit period removes the formal check that conditions remain safe to continue.

column1: Job was paused and the permit was formally re-validated after a shift handover introduced a new work crew to the site.
column4: The re-validation step ensured the new crew was briefed and conditions were reconfirmed safe.

column1: Worker began isolating a valve on a live line based on a verbal instruction from a colleague, without a written permit or isolation certificate.
column4: Verbal-only authorization on a live system removes formal checks designed to prevent working on the wrong or unisolated equipment.

column1: Simultaneous operations form was completed and reviewed before scaffolding work began near an active crane lift zone.
column4: Coordination between the two activities was formally reviewed and managed before work began.

column1: Employee received a minor cut while filling out permit-required paperwork on a clipboard with a sharp edge before starting an authorized job.
column4: The injury was unrelated to the job hazard itself and occurred during an otherwise correctly authorized process.

column1: Two separate crews were both issued permits for overlapping work on the same pipe section without either being made aware of the other.
column4: Uncoordinated simultaneous work on the same equipment can result in one crew being exposed to hazards created by the other.

column1: Permit was issued for hot work but did not specify that a nearby vent was still connected to the process, work proceeded on this basis.
column4: An incomplete permit hazard assessment left a live connection unaccounted for, risking ignition of process vapors.

column1: Supervisor conducted a pre-job toolbox talk covering permit conditions and site-specific hazards before releasing the crew to start work.
column4: Clear communication of authorized scope and hazards reduced the chance of unauthorized or unsafe deviations.

column1: Worker leaned out from a scaffold platform without a harness to reach a fitting slightly out of arm's reach; did not fall.
column4: Leaning beyond a guarded platform edge without fall protection carries high fatal potential regardless of this outcome.

column1: Full-body harness was worn and correctly anchored to an approved point before work began on an elevated platform above six metres.
column4: Fall protection was correctly used, controlling the primary hazard of working at height.

column1: Employee used a stepladder on uneven ground without securing it, ladder wobbled but the worker regained balance and did not fall.
column4: An unsecured ladder on uneven ground is a well-known precursor to falls from height, regardless of whether this attempt ended safely.

column1: Scaffold was inspected and tagged by a competent person before use, with guardrails and toe boards confirmed in place.
column4: Standard scaffold inspection and guarding controls were verified before workers accessed the structure.

column1: Worker climbed onto an elevated pipe rack without a harness to inspect a fitting, standing approximately four metres above ground level.
column4: Unprotected access to an elevated structure at this height carries a high risk of fatal fall.

column1: Employee received a minor scrape to the forearm while descending a properly secured and inspected ladder, following all access procedures correctly.
column4: An injury occurred, but proper fall-protection procedures were followed and the height/energy involved was low.

column1: Roof access hatch was left open and unguarded near a walking path for several hours during a maintenance job, no one approached the opening.
column4: An open, unguarded fall hazard on a walked route creates ongoing potential for a fatal fall regardless of whether anyone approached it during this period.

column1: Guardrails were temporarily removed to move materials onto a platform, and were reinstalled immediately before any personnel accessed the area again.
column4: The fall hazard was controlled by sequencing the work so no personnel were exposed while guarding was down.

column1: Two workers stood on the top rung of a stepladder, above the manufacturer's rated standing line, to reach an overhead cable tray.
column4: Standing above the rated line significantly increases the chance of losing balance and falling from an unstable position.

column1: Fall arrest system was inspected before the shift and a worker's harness was found to have a damaged D-ring; harness was replaced before work began.
column4: The defect was identified and corrected before any exposure to a fall occurred.

column1: A crane operator swung a loaded pallet directly over two technicians working on the ground below.
column3: Line of Fire; Safe Mechanical Lifting
column4: Positioning a suspended load directly above personnel exposes them to a potentially fatal strike if the load or rigging fails.

column1: Employee stood beneath an overhead crane hook while it repositioned a large steel beam across the yard.
column3: Line of Fire; Safe Mechanical Lifting
column4: Standing under a moving overhead load is a direct exposure to a heavy falling-object hazard.

column1: Rigger walked underneath a raised excavator bucket to reach tools on the far side of the site.
column4: Passing beneath a raised, heavy piece of equipment exposes the worker to being crushed if it drops or swings unexpectedly.

column1: A technician reached up to adjust a sling while a suspended engine block hung directly above his head.
column3: Line of Fire; Safe Mechanical Lifting
column4: Working directly beneath a suspended heavy object puts the worker in the direct path of a fatal strike if the load shifts.

column1: Two workers paused for a break in the shade cast by a crane's suspended concrete slab overhead.
column3: Line of Fire; Safe Mechanical Lifting
column4: Remaining under a suspended load for any reason, including incidentally, carries the same fatal strike potential as working there.

column1: A forklift carried a raised pallet of pipe fittings across a walkway while a pedestrian passed directly beneath the forks.
column4: A raised load passing over a pedestrian is a direct line-of-fire exposure to a falling-object strike.

column1: Maintenance crew stood under a gantry crane's load path to guide a hanging valve assembly into position by hand.
column3: Line of Fire; Safe Mechanical Lifting
column4: Manually guiding a load from directly beneath it removes any margin of safety if the load drops.

column1: A worker crossed under an active tower crane's boom line to shortcut to the site office, without checking for an ongoing lift.
column3: Line of Fire; Safe Mechanical Lifting
column4: Crossing beneath an active crane's load path exposes a person to being struck without warning by a load or falling rigging.

column1: The crane's exclusion zone was clearly marked and no personnel entered the area beneath the suspended load during the entire lift.
column4: Maintaining the exclusion zone meant no one was ever exposed to the suspended load overhead.

column1: Load was lifted only after all personnel moved outside the marked barrier line surrounding the lift area.
column3: Line of Fire; Safe Mechanical Lifting
column4: Personnel were cleared from the hazard zone before the lift began, removing any exposure to the suspended load.

column1: A pallet was lifted two feet off the ground to check the forklift's hydraulics, with no one within ten metres of the load.
column4: Minimal lift height and complete absence of nearby personnel meant no meaningful exposure existed.

column1: Driver scraped a traffic cone while parking at speed.
column4: Low speed maneuver.

column1: Vehicle involved in a parking-lot scrape with a bollard while reversing at parking speed.
column4: Stationary object involved meant low risk of serious injury.

column1: Employee stepped on the first rung of a ladder without tying off but stepped down immediately.
column4: Very low height and minimal fall risk.

column1: Full-body harness was worn and correctly anchored before work began on an elevated platform.
column4: Fall protection was used and controlled the hazard.

column1: Scaffold was inspected and tagged by a competent person before use.
column4: Standard scaffold inspection and guarding controls were verified.

column1: Guardrails were temporarily removed and reinstalled before personnel accessed the area.
column4: No personnel were exposed while guarding was removed.

column1: Fall arrest system inspection found a damaged harness which was replaced before work began.
column4: The defect was identified and corrected before exposure occurred.

column1: Employee received a scrape while descending a secured ladder.
column4: Fall protection procedures were followed.

column1: Worker received static shock while inspecting equipment after lockout.
column4: Energy was mostly isolated resulting in localized shock.

column1: Crew completed full lockout/tagout with verification before opening equipment.
column4: All required isolation steps were performed and verified.

column1: Electrician removed an old lockout tag after confirming the job was complete.
column4: Verification was performed before removing the tag.

column1: Worker received a pinch while rotating an isolated valve wheel.
column4: Equipment was isolated and no hazardous energy was present.

column1: Operator touched a de-energized breaker panel after full LOTO verification.
column4: Isolation and verification had already been completed.

column1: Spark from handheld grinder burned a hole in a glove.
column4: Equipment damage with no significant fire or injury potential.

column1: Hot work permit was issued and all controls were in place before welding.
column4: All required controls were verified before work started.

column1: Flashback arrestor was inspected and confirmed functional before hot work.
column4: Equipment safeguards were verified functional.

column1: Worker sustained a finger burn from a hot weld bead while using PPE.
column4: Localized contact injury with major controls in place.

column1: Team relocated a hot work job after identifying nearby flammable vapor sources.
column4: Hazard was identified and removed before work began.

column1: Worker dropped a wrench from waist level and narrowly missed a foot.
column4: Dropped object carried low fatality potential.
